CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR VICTIMS OF GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

Gender-based violence and violence against children is a social phenomenon that has existed since ancient times and has become increasingly prevalent recently. In fact, gender-based violence and violence against children continue to increase, both in number and in the form and modus operandi which are increasingly diverse. Rape, sexual harassment, trafficking of women and children, domestic violence, sexual exploitation, violence against domestic workers, pornography, exploitation of migrant workers, and neglect, will apparently continue to be encountered in daily life, both in the domestic (household) and public spheres.

The causal factors of gender-based violence and violence against children are very complex and interrelated. These factors include, among others, legal instruments that have not been able to provide protection to victims, the concept that women and children are family property (assets), media that do not adequately support reporting on violence against women and children, public services that are not yet optimal, customs that sometimes legalize violence, poverty issues, misinterpretation of religious teachings, all of which are wrapped in a patriarchal culture.

The handling of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children occurring in Ogan Komering Ulu Regency, in accordance with the provisions of Article 13 of Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, requires that Regional Governments establish and develop a system and mechanism of cooperation for handling violence. Furthermore, based on the provisions of Article 26 paragraph (1) letter b of Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government, it states that the Deputy Regional Head has the duty to assist the Regional Head in coordinating the activities of vertical institutions in the region, following up on reports and/or findings of supervisory apparatus oversight, implementing women's and youth empowerment, and endeavoring to develop and preserve social culture and the environment. Therefore, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 21

(1) In implementing protection for victims of gender-based and child violence, regional governments may cooperate with the Government, other Regional Governments.

(2) Cooperation between Regional Governments and the Government includes consultation, coordination and reporting.

(3) Cooperation between Regional Governments and other Regional Governments includes coordination, advocacy, referrals, repatriation, social reintegration and development of integrated service systems.

Article 25

(1) Control, guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children shall be carried out by the Regent, the implementation of which is carried out by the Vice Regent.

(2) The implementation of control, guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out daily by the SKPD responsible for women's empowerment affairs and child protection.

Article 11

Legal protection as referred to in Article 8 includes:

a. providing protection in safe houses (shelters);
b. providing assistance in legal proceedings at the high court level; and
c. providing special legal protection for child victims of violence may be conducted through the appointment of guardianship in accordance with applicable regulations.

Paragraph 3

Legal Protection

Article 24

(1) To prevent acts of violence against women and children, Regional Governments shall conduct socialization, empowerment, and awareness raising to families, parents, and communities by providing information, guidance and/or counseling.

(2) In addition to empowerment and awareness raising as referred to in paragraph (1), Regional Governments shall undertake efforts as follows:

a. increasing the quantity and quality of education both formal and non-formal and informal;
b. opening employment opportunities for women;
c. building community participation and awareness toward the prevention and protection of women and children from acts of violence; and
d. building networks and cooperation with law enforcement officers, government officials, universities and various non-governmental organizations that work in and/or care about women and children.

Article 6

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR VICTIMS OF GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

Gender-based violence and violence against children is a social phenomenon that has existed since ancient times and has become increasingly prevalent recently. In fact, gender-based violence and violence against children continue to increase, both in number and in the form and modus operandi which are increasingly diverse. Rape, sexual harassment, trafficking of women and children, domestic violence, sexual exploitation, violence against domestic workers, pornography, exploitation of migrant workers, and neglect, will apparently continue to be encountered in daily life, both in the domestic (household) and public spheres.

The causal factors of gender-based violence and violence against children are very complex and interrelated. These factors include, among others, legal instruments that have not been able to provide protection to victims, the concept that women and children are family property (assets), media that do not adequately support reporting on violence against women and children, public services that are not yet optimal, customs that sometimes legalize violence, poverty issues, misinterpretation of religious teachings, all of which are wrapped in a patriarchal culture.

The handling of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children occurring in Ogan Komering Ulu Regency, in accordance with the provisions of Article 13 of Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, requires that Regional Governments establish and develop a system and mechanism of cooperation for handling violence. Furthermore, based on the provisions of Article 26 paragraph (1) letter b of Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government, it states that the Deputy Regional Head has the duty to assist the Regional Head in coordinating the activities of vertical institutions in the region, following up on reports and/or findings of supervisory apparatus oversight, implementing women's and youth empowerment, and endeavoring to develop and preserve social culture and the environment. Therefore, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 24

(1) To prevent acts of violence against women and children, Regional Governments shall conduct socialization, empowerment, and awareness raising to families, parents, and communities by providing information, guidance and/or counseling.

(2) In addition to empowerment and awareness raising as referred to in paragraph (1), Regional Governments shall undertake efforts as follows:

a. increasing the quantity and quality of education both formal and non-formal and informal;
b. opening employment opportunities for women;
c. building community participation and awareness toward the prevention and protection of women and children from acts of violence; and
d. building networks and cooperation with law enforcement officers, government officials, universities and various non-governmental organizations that work in and/or care about women and children.

Article 2

Letter a

What is meant by "non-discrimination" is protection for all victims of gender-based violence and violence against children without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status and physical or mental condition.

Letter b

What is meant by "best interests of the victim" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, community, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, the best interests of the victim must be a primary consideration.

Letter c

What is meant by "gender justice" is fair treatment given to women and men. What is meant by "gender equality" is a condition and position that describes harmonious, appropriate and balanced relations between men and women in obtaining opportunities/opportunities in access, participation, control and benefits in development implementation and enjoying development outcomes in family life, as well as in community, national and state life.

Letter d

What is meant by "victim protection" is providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family members, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.

Letter e

What is meant by "maternal survival" is ensuring that a mother does not experience death that occurs during pregnancy, childbirth, and postpartum, whether caused by physical or non-physical conditions. Letter f

What is meant by "growth and development" of children is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to education, the right to play, the right to create and recreate.

What is meant by "survival" of children is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to identity and the right to enjoy the highest attainable health status.

Letter g

What is meant by "respect for the views of the child" is respect for children's rights to participate and express their opinions in decision-making, especially if it concerns matters that affect their lives.

Letter h

What is meant by "openness" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children, it is transparent among integrated service providers and KPK2BGA.

Letter i

What is meant by "integration" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children, it is implemented by building coordination among service providers, including medical services, legal advocates, psychologists, clergy, social workers, police.

Letter j

What is meant by "not blaming the victim" is an attitude and treatment of not blaming the victim for the occurrence of the violence they experienced.

Letter k

What is meant by "empowering" is that every effort provided must be able to strengthen victims, whether physically, psychologically, socially or economically.

Letter l

What is meant by "victim confidentiality" is every action taken to ensure that victims are in a safe condition from threats or other actions that threaten the life and psychology of victims.

Letter m

What is meant by "decision-making in the hands of the victim" is the victim's right to determine the best choice in resolving their problem.

Article 25

(1) Control, guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children shall be carried out by the Regent, the implementation of which is carried out by the Vice Regent.

(2) The implementation of control, guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out daily by the SKPD responsible for women's empowerment affairs and child protection.

Article 21

(1) In implementing protection for victims of gender-based and child violence, regional governments may cooperate with the Government, other Regional Governments.

(2) Cooperation between Regional Governments and the Government includes consultation, coordination and reporting.

(3) Cooperation between Regional Governments and other Regional Governments includes coordination, advocacy, referrals, repatriation, social reintegration and development of integrated service systems.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms mean:

1. Central Government hereinafter referred to as Government is the President of the Republic of Indonesia who holds the power of the Government of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
2. Region is the Regency of Ogan Komering Ulu.
3. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as the element organizing regional government.
4. Regent is the Regent of Ogan Komering Ulu.
5. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb as referred to in Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.
6. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can change due to the social and cultural conditions of society.
7. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutor's office, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court order.
8. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
9. Implementation of protection is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the Commission for the Protection of Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children, and the Integrated Service Center.
10. Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, distinction and all forms of treatment conducted on the basis of gender and aimed at reducing, eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights, the consequences of which include and are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
11. Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, distinction, exclusion and all forms of treatment conducted against children, the consequences of which include and are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological, and economic violence.
12. Victims of Gender-based Violence are persons who because of their gender experience physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses caused by state policy, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
13. Child Victims of Violence are children who receive harsh treatment whether physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual, and other losses caused by state policy, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
14. Victim Recovery is all efforts to empower victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physical, psychological, social, economic or sexual.
15. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems faced.
16. Commission for the Protection of Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children hereinafter referred to as KPK2BGA is the Commission for the Protection of Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children of Ogan Komering Ulu Regency established by the Regent which is a non-structural commission.
17. Integrated Services is a series of activities to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unit of implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal aid for victims of gender-based violence and children.
18. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes who can provide protection and fulfillment of victim needs.
19. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with established operational standards.

Article 26

All activities related to the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children shall be charged to the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of the Regency.

Article 11

Legal protection as referred to in Article 8 includes:

b. providing assistance in legal proceedings at the high court level; and
c. providing special legal protection for child victims of violence may be conducted through the appointment of guardianship in accordance with applicable regulations.

Article 28

(1) At the time this Regional Regulation comes into force, all implementing regulations related to the protection of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children shall remain in force insofar as they do not conflict with and/or have not been replaced by new regulations.

(2) The Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) of Ogan Komering Ulu Regency that has been established before this Regional Regulation comes into force shall remain recognized.

In implementing protection for victims of gender-based violence and child victims of violence, the Regional Government is assisted by: a. Integrated Services; and

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR VICTIMS OF GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

Gender-based violence and violence against children is a social phenomenon that has existed since ancient times and has become increasingly prevalent recently. In fact, gender-based violence and violence against children continue to increase, both in number and in the form and modus operandi which are increasingly diverse. Rape, sexual harassment, trafficking of women and children, domestic violence, sexual exploitation, violence against domestic workers, pornography, exploitation of migrant workers, and neglect, will apparently continue to be encountered in daily life, both in the domestic (household) and public spheres.

The causal factors of gender-based violence and violence against children are very complex and interrelated. These factors include, among others, legal instruments that have not been able to provide protection to victims, the concept that women and children are family property (assets), media that do not adequately support reporting on violence against women and children, public services that are not yet optimal, customs that sometimes legalize violence, poverty issues, misinterpretation of religious teachings, all of which are wrapped in a patriarchal culture.

The handling of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children occurring in Ogan Komering Ulu Regency, in accordance with the provisions of Article 13 of Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, requires that Regional Governments establish and develop a system and mechanism of cooperation for handling violence. Furthermore, based on the provisions of Article 26 paragraph (1) letter b of Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government, it states that the Deputy Regional Head has the duty to assist the Regional Head in coordinating the activities of vertical institutions in the region, following up on reports and/or findings of supervisory apparatus oversight, implementing women's and youth empowerment, and endeavoring to develop and preserve social culture and the environment. Therefore, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children.

Article 2

Letter a

What is meant by "non-discrimination" is protection for all victims of gender-based violence and violence against children without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status and physical or mental condition.

Letter b

What is meant by "best interests of the victim" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, community, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, the best interests of the victim must be a primary consideration.

Letter c

What is meant by "gender justice" is fair treatment given to women and men. What is meant by "gender equality" is a condition and position that describes harmonious, appropriate and balanced relations between men and women in obtaining opportunities/opportunities in access, participation, control and benefits in development implementation and enjoying development outcomes in family life, as well as in community, national and state life.

Letter d

What is meant by "victim protection" is providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family members, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.

Letter e

What is meant by "maternal survival" is ensuring that a mother does not experience death that occurs during pregnancy, childbirth, and postpartum, whether caused by physical or non-physical conditions. Letter f

What is meant by "growth and development" of children is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to education, the right to play, the right to create and recreate.

What is meant by "survival" of children is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to identity and the right to enjoy the highest attainable health status.

Letter g

What is meant by "respect for the views of the child" is respect for children's rights to participate and express their opinions in decision-making, especially if it concerns matters that affect their lives.

Letter h

What is meant by "openness" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children, it is transparent among integrated service providers and KPK2BGA.

Letter i

What is meant by "integration" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children, it is implemented by building coordination among service providers, including medical services, legal advocates, psychologists, clergy, social workers, police.

Letter j

What is meant by "not blaming the victim" is an attitude and treatment of not blaming the victim for the occurrence of the violence they experienced.

Letter k

What is meant by "empowering" is that every effort provided must be able to strengthen victims, whether physically, psychologically, socially or economically.

Letter l

What is meant by "victim confidentiality" is every action taken to ensure that victims are in a safe condition from threats or other actions that threaten the life and psychology of victims.

Letter m

What is meant by "decision-making in the hands of the victim" is the victim's right to determine the best choice in resolving their problem.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR VICTIMS OF GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

Gender-based violence and violence against children is a social phenomenon that has existed since ancient times and has become increasingly prevalent recently. In fact, gender-based violence and violence against children continue to increase, both in number and in the form and modus operandi which are increasingly diverse. Rape, sexual harassment, trafficking of women and children, domestic violence, sexual exploitation, violence against domestic workers, pornography, exploitation of migrant workers, and neglect, will apparently continue to be encountered in daily life, both in the domestic (household) and public spheres.

The causal factors of gender-based violence and violence against children are very complex and interrelated. These factors include, among others, legal instruments that have not been able to provide protection to victims, the concept that women and children are family property (assets), media that do not adequately support reporting on violence against women and children, public services that are not yet optimal, customs that sometimes legalize violence, poverty issues, misinterpretation of religious teachings, all of which are wrapped in a patriarchal culture.

The handling of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children occurring in Ogan Komering Ulu Regency, in accordance with the provisions of Article 13 of Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, requires that Regional Governments establish and develop a system and mechanism of cooperation for handling violence. Furthermore, based on the provisions of Article 26 paragraph (1) letter b of Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government, it states that the Deputy Regional Head has the duty to assist the Regional Head in coordinating the activities of vertical institutions in the region, following up on reports and/or findings of supervisory apparatus oversight, implementing women's and youth empowerment, and endeavoring to develop and preserve social culture and the environment. Therefore, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms mean:

1. Central Government hereinafter referred to as Government is the President of the Republic of Indonesia who holds the power of the Government of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
2. Region is the Regency of Ogan Komering Ulu.
3. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as the element organizing regional government.
4. Regent is the Regent of Ogan Komering Ulu.
5. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb as referred to in Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.
6. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can change due to the social and cultural conditions of society.
7. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutor's office, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court order.
8. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
9. Implementation of protection is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the Commission for the Protection of Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children, and the Integrated Service Center.
10. Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, distinction and all forms of treatment conducted on the basis of gender and aimed at reducing, eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights, the consequences of which include and are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
11. Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, distinction, exclusion and all forms of treatment conducted against children, the consequences of which include and are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological, and economic violence.
12. Victims of Gender-based Violence are persons who because of their gender experience physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses caused by state policy, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
13. Child Victims of Violence are children who receive harsh treatment whether physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual, and other losses caused by state policy, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
14. Victim Recovery is all efforts to empower victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physical, psychological, social, economic or sexual.
15. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems faced.
16. Commission for the Protection of Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children hereinafter referred to as KPK2BGA is the Commission for the Protection of Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children of Ogan Komering Ulu Regency established by the Regent which is a non-structural commission.
17. Integrated Services is a series of activities to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unit of implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal aid for victims of gender-based violence and children.
18. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes who can provide protection and fulfillment of victim needs.
19. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with established operational standards.

Article 7

(1) Integrated services as referred to in Article 6 letter a shall be established by the Regional Government in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.

(2) The establishment of integrated services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall consist of members from regional government elements, non-governmental institutions, health service institutions, law enforcement officers, professional personnel, companion volunteers, social workers, clergy, safe houses (shelters), and social rehabilitation centers.

Article 2

Letter a

What is meant by "non-discrimination" is protection for all victims of gender-based violence and violence against children without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status and physical or mental condition.

Letter b

What is meant by "best interests of the victim" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, community, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, the best interests of the victim must be a primary consideration.

Letter c

What is meant by "gender justice" is fair treatment given to women and men. What is meant by "gender equality" is a condition and position that describes harmonious, appropriate and balanced relations between men and women in obtaining opportunities/opportunities in access, participation, control and benefits in development implementation and enjoying development outcomes in family life, as well as in community, national and state life.

Letter d

What is meant by "victim protection" is providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family members, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.

Letter e

What is meant by "maternal survival" is ensuring that a mother does not experience death that occurs during pregnancy, childbirth, and postpartum, whether caused by physical or non-physical conditions. Letter f

What is meant by "growth and development" of children is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to education, the right to play, the right to create and recreate.

What is meant by "survival" of children is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to identity and the right to enjoy the highest attainable health status.

Letter g

What is meant by "respect for the views of the child" is respect for children's rights to participate and express their opinions in decision-making, especially if it concerns matters that affect their lives.

Letter h

What is meant by "openness" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children, it is transparent among integrated service providers and KPK2BGA.

Letter i

What is meant by "integration" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children, it is implemented by building coordination among service providers, including medical services, legal advocates, psychologists, clergy, social workers, police.

Letter j

What is meant by "not blaming the victim" is an attitude and treatment of not blaming the victim for the occurrence of the violence they experienced.

Letter k

What is meant by "empowering" is that every effort provided must be able to strengthen victims, whether physically, psychologically, socially or economically.

Letter l

What is meant by "victim confidentiality" is every action taken to ensure that victims are in a safe condition from threats or other actions that threaten the life and psychology of victims.

Letter m

What is meant by "decision-making in the hands of the victim" is the victim's right to determine the best choice in resolving their problem.
